description: Public edition: Designs and controls manufacturing processes that position atoms or molecular units with extreme precision.
body:
Atomic-Precision Construction Engine. Designs and controls manufacturing processes that position atoms or molecular units with extreme precision.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 21 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Matter Manipulation and Molecular Manufacturing". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. STM atom manipulation (Eigler, 1990) and DNA origami place matter precisely; general atom-by-atom manufacturing of products remains out of reach.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Atomic-Precision Construction Engine - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Designs and controls manufacturing processes that position atoms or molecular units with extreme precision.
body:
Known science foundations of Atomic-Precision Construction Engine.

Don Eigler positioned 35 xenon atoms to spell IBM in 1990. DNA origami (Rothemund, 2006) folds DNA into designed shapes. Dip-pen nanolithography patterns molecules. Scanning-probe atom placement is serial and slow. Drexler's molecular-manufacturing proposals remain theoretical; no general assembler exists.

Key quantity check (Atoms placed per hour by one STM tip / atoms in a 1 mm^3 product): computed ratio 1e-17 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Atomic-Precision Construction Engine - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Designs and controls manufacturing processes that position atoms or molecular units with extreme precision.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Atomic-Precision Construction Engine.

Serial atom placement is far too slow for macroscopic products. Thermal noise fights precision at room temperature. Designing build sequences for arbitrary products is unsolved.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 29 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is atoms in 1 mm^3 vs placement precision at 29 orders of magnitude (atoms in 1 mm^3 larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Atomic-Precision Construction Engine - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: Designs and controls manufacturing processes that position atoms or molecular units with extreme precision.
body:
Unresolved problems for Atomic-Precision Construction Engine, in priority order (research burden index 30, 3 blocking):

Parallelizing placement to useful throughput (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

Room-temperature atomic precision (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

From placement to functional product (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

What would count as evidence of success for Atomic-Precision Construction Engine:

Places 1,000 atoms with <0.1 nm error (weight 0.4; SATISFIED).

Assembles a functional device atom-by-atom (weight 0.35; not yet satisfied).

Reaches 1 mm^3/day throughput (weight 0.25; not yet satisfied).

Evidence confidence: 0.4 (1 of 3 criteria satisfied). Verdict: partial. Confidence here measures satisfied evidence, not belief.
